content: The coadministration of certain drugs with hydroxyzine can lead to significant pharmacodynamic interactions, which may result in increased sedation, QTc interval prolongation, or other adverse effects. Below are the detailed interactions and their clinical implications: 1. Coadministration of hydroxyzine with CNS depressants increases the risk of central nervous system depression, potentially leading to additive psychomotor impairment and daytime dysfunction. Close monitoring is required. 2. Dasatinib and hydroxyzine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Hydroxyzine and daxibotulinumtoxinA exhibit pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the effects of the botulinum toxin. Use caution and monitor closely. Drugs with anticholinergic effects may potentiate botulinum toxin effects, leading to excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. 4. Degarelix and hydroxyzine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Desflurane and hydroxyzine increase sedation. Avoid or use alternative drugs due to the risk of serious additive sedation. Both also prolong the QTc interval, necessitating avoidance or alternative therapy. 6. Hydroxyzine and desipramine increase sedation and prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Desloratadine and hydroxyzine increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Deutetrabenazine and hydroxyzine increase sedation and prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not clinically prolong the QT interval, but certain conditions may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death. 9. Dexbrompheniramine and hydroxyzine increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Dexchlorpheniramine and hydroxyzine increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Hydroxyzine increases sedation, while dexfenfluramine decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor closely. 12. Dexmedetomidine and hydroxyzine increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Hydroxyzine increases sedation, while dexmethylphenidate decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor closely. 14. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Hydroxyzine and erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate) increase QTc interval prolongation and the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Hydroxyzine and escitalopram both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 38.
